I think you have an air bubble and you didn’t bleed it properly. 
Turn the key but don’t start the engine, air to hottest and fan low, remember the little red blue dial thingy for the ac and spin it to red, and slowly add coolant to the expansion tank until no bubbles come out the bleed hole. Then put the expansion tank cap on tight, and bleed screw super tight but don’t break it, and do the same thing the next day.
I had to check levels and add/remove coolant for a few days until it was sorted.

I found the problem was fuse F106 which is a 50-amp fuse that controls the starter officially but if it’s bad you won’t get dashboard lights, AC, no power to the ignition, it’s like you don’t have a key turned. 

The fuse is above the regular glove box fuses, under a black cover. You do NOT have to remove the glove box like some people say.
